questions.e: The common divisors of 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3 and 6; the largest is 6.
Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12… and of 6: 6, 12… The first common one is 12.

questions.q: Why write a / gcd(a, b) * b instead of a * b / gcd(a, b)?
o: The product a × b can overflow before the division
Division must always come first in C++
questions.e: Both formulas are equal on paper, but a × b can be far larger than the LCM and overflow. Dividing first keeps the numbers small.

questions.q: A loop that finds the GCD of an array should start at:
questions.e: gcd(0, x) = x, so 0 doesn't change the answer. Starting at 1 always gives 1. (An LCM loop starts at 1.)

questions.q: Two lights blink every 4 s and 6 s, together at time 0. When do they next blink together?
questions.e: “Together again” is the smallest time both periods divide: lcm(4, 6) = 12.

questions.q: With jugs of 4 and 6 litres, which total can you measure exactly?
questions.e: Reachable totals are the multiples of gcd(4, 6) = 2 that are at most 4 + 6 = 10. Only 8 is both.
The differences from 5 are 12, 18 and 6, and their gcd is 6. That is the largest k for which all four numbers leave the same remainder.
